from.place: ## Proof, affine case: the sentence identifying H^q(C_et,G_m) with H^q(Cbar_et,j_*G_m) from the Leray spectral sequence

title: Low-degree Leray comparison for an open immersion
statement: Let j:C \to Cbar be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion] and let F be an abelian sheaf on the small etale site of C [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. If (R^q j_*F)_x=0 for every geometric point x of Cbar [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] and q=1,2, then the natural Leray edge map H^q(Cbar_et,j_*F) \to H^q(C_et,F) in etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], formed using the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], is an isomorphism for q=0,1,2.

source.place: Discussion preceding Tag 03RM; low-degree consequence of the Leray spectral sequence after vanishing of R^1j_*F and R^2j_*F

proof.text: The hypotheses that (R^1 j_*F)_x and (R^2 j_*F)_x vanish at every geometric point imply R^1 j_*F=0 and R^2 j_*F=0 by conservativity of geometric stalks [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative].

Apply the Grothendieck spectral sequence [thm-sp-grothendieck] to the composable left-exact functors j_* and Gamma(Cbar,-). The etale direct image j_* preserves injective sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives], so it sends injectives to Gamma(Cbar,-)-acyclic objects. By the definition of etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and the identity Gamma(Cbar,j_*F)=Gamma(C,F) from the definition of direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the E_2 terms are H^p(Cbar_et,R^q j_*F) and the abutment is H^{p+q}(C_et,F). The bottom edge map of [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps] is the natural Leray edge map in the statement.

source.place: Discussion preceding Tag 03RM; Leray spectral sequence

proof.text: In total degree n<=2, the only rows other than q=0 are q=1 and q=2, which vanish by Step 1. Differentials entering E_r^{n,0} originate in row q=r-1; for r=2,3 these are zero and for r>=4 their first coordinate n-r is negative. Differentials leaving row q=0 land at negative q. Hence E_2^{n,0}=E_infty^{n,0}. The finite filtration from Step 2 has no other nonzero graded piece in degree n, so F^nH^n=H^n and its bottom edge map is an isomorphism for n=0,1,2.

lean.statement: theorem openCurveEtaleLerayLowDegree {C Cbar : Scheme.{u}} (j : C ⟶ Cbar) [IsOpenImmersion j] (F : Sheaf C.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (hvanish : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Cbar) (q : ℤ), (q = 1 ∨ q = 2) → IsZero ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale x).sheafFiber.obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Sheaf Cbar.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) q).obj ((Etale.rightDerivedLowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} j).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf C.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) 0).obj F))))) : ∀ q : ℕ, (q = 0 ∨ q = 1 ∨ q = 2) → Function.Bijective fun x : Sheaf.H ((Etale.lowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} j).obj F) q ↦ Sheaf.H.map ((Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} j).counit.app F) q (Etale.cohomologyMap j _ q x)
lean.note: Second reading: asserts bijectivity of the canonical Leray edge map (cohomologyMap followed by the counit), using the existing Sheaf.H Ext model of abelian sheaf cohomology. The cohomology definition node explicitly permits this model with the derived-global-sections identification deferred to stage 3. Stalkwise vanishing uses the recorded derived direct image on a sheaf in degree zero.
